confirmed.title: judgeIO classifies Windows media errors (not ready / CRC / read-write fault / general failure) as PermissionDenied = Deterministic, so drive-wait never engages for them
confirmed.summary: judgeIO puts every PermissionDenied IOException in the Deterministic family and never checks whether the drive is present. On Windows, GHC's errno mapping (the CRT/base _dosmaperr EACCES range ERROR_WRITE_PROTECT..ERROR_SHARING_BUFFER_EXCEEDED, 19..36) turns the device-state errors ERROR_NOT_READY 21, ERROR_CRC 23, ERROR_WRITE_FAULT 29, ERROR_READ_FAULT 30 and ERROR_GEN_FAILURE 31 into PermissionDenied. When a USB backup drive drops and the first escaping exception carries one of these codes, execPlanRetry and withDriveRetry rethrow it at once with no wait and no retry. That is the 1.1.1 behaviour the 1.1.2 drive-wait protection was built to remove.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `pm backup` or a GUI apply of a backup plan (drive-wait armed, default 1800 s) is copying to the USB drive. The drive enters its removal/re-arrival transition. copyFileHashed's Win32 createFile of the tmp (openExclusiveBinary), a BS.hPut, or Win32 flushFileBuffers fails with ERROR_NOT_READY (21) or ERROR_GEN_FAILURE (31). The IOException has type PermissionDenied and escapes execPlan (write-side escape = process-death semantics). In execPlanRetry, judgeIO returns Deterministic, recover returns False, and throwIO e fires. The run aborts immediately, leaving C1/C2 journal holes, and has to be re-run by hand, even though the drive would have come back seconds later. If the same drop surfaces as EINVAL (the one form observed on 2026-09-02) it is handled correctly, so whether protection works depends on which Win32 code the dying device returns.
confirmed.evidence: Removable.hs:110-116: `judgeIO root e | t `elem` [UserError, PermissionDenied, AlreadyExists, IllegalOperation, InappropriateType, UnsupportedOperation] = pure Deterministic | otherwise = do ok <- driveOk root; pure (if not ok then Dropped else ...)`. The drive is consulted only for the non-deterministic family. execPlanRetry at Removable.hs:246-254: `Left e | n >= dwAttempts dw -> throwIO e | otherwise -> do v <- judgeIO root e; ok <- recover dw root "执行" v (show e); unless ok (throwIO e)`, and recover returns False for Deterministic (line 137). Write path: Exec.execCopyTmp -> Hash.copyFileHashed (Hash.hs:154-166: openFreshBinary dst -> Win32File.createFile; BS.hPut; flushHandleToDisk -> Win32File.flushFileBuffers). Probe run on this machine (GHC 9.10.3, `System.Win32.Types.failWith "probe" c` then ioe_type): 21 -> permission denied, 23 -> permission denied, 29 -> permission denied, 30 -> permission denied, 31 -> permission denied, 32 -> permission denied (compare 87/1006/1167 -> invalid argument, 2/3 -> does not exist). The DESIGN §6.4 / DESIGN-COMMANDS text lists 权限 as deterministic on the assumption that it means an ACL refusal; neither REVIEW-LOG nor the known-findings JSON covers this mapping. Suggested direction: for PermissionDenied, still answer Dropped when driveOk is False. With the drive present the result stays Deterministic, so RemovableTests caseDeterministic (PermissionDenied with drive present) is unaffected.

verdict.reasoning: Code: Removable.hs:112 puts PermissionDenied in the Deterministic set before driveOk is ever consulted. recover returns False for Deterministic (line 137). execPlanRetry then runs `unless ok (throwIO e)` at line 254, and withDriveRetry/scanRootRetry run `throwIO e` at lines 173/210. Library check: I ran a read-only probe with the repo's GHC via `stack exec -- runghc -package=Win32` on System.Win32.Types.failWith. It gave 19/21/23/29/30/31/32 -> permission denied and 87/121/433/1006/1117/1167 -> invalid argument. The Handle write path (BS.hPut on the handle from hANDLEToHandle under the default MIO manager) goes through the CRT, whose _dosmaperr EACCES range 19..36 gives the same mapping. Win32File.flushFileBuffers and createFile (Win.hs:112, :535) go through failWith directly. So a backup-drive write that fails with ERROR_NOT_READY (21) or ERROR_GEN_FAILURE (31), or a read that fails with ERROR_CRC (23) or ERROR_READ_FAULT (30), becomes PermissionDenied. Trace: `pm backup` with drive-wait 1800. The drive resets during copyFileHashed (Hash.hs:154-166), and flushHandleToDisk's FlushFileBuffers fails with 31. The IOException (PermissionDenied) escapes execPlan. In execPlanRetry (n=0 < 5), judgeIO gives Deterministic and recover gives False, so throwIO fires with no wait and no heal. That is the 1.1.1 abort the feature was meant to remove. Design check: REVIEW-LOG.md:599 and DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:312 list 权限 as deterministic only on the stated rationale of ACL refusals (withDenyAll, pm's own fail-closed refusals). Neither mentions that Win32 device-state codes map to PermissionDenied, so this is an unexamined assumption rather than a ruling on this case. Not in the known-findings JSON: the only PermissionDenied item there, the refuted Config.hs:654 lock-contention one, is about something else. Limits: the observed 2026-09-02 drops surfaced as EINVAL, as do the common removal codes 1006, 1117 and 1167, and those are handled. The failure needs the device to return one of the 19..36 codes, which makes it an edge path. No data is lost: the journal holes are recoverable by doctor and a re-run.
verdict.corrected_summary: On Windows, GHC maps Win32 errors 19..36 (including ERROR_NOT_READY 21, ERROR_CRC 23, ERROR_WRITE_FAULT 29, ERROR_READ_FAULT 30 and ERROR_GEN_FAILURE 31) to PermissionDenied, confirmed by probe. judgeIO classifies every PermissionDenied as Deterministic without checking the drive. When a flaky USB backup drive fails with one of these codes, execPlanRetry, withDriveRetry and scanRootRetry therefore rethrow at once with no wait or retry, and drive-wait protection only works for drops that surface as EINVAL-class codes.
verdict.suggested_fix: In judgeIO, stop classifying PermissionDenied as unconditionally deterministic. When the type is PermissionDenied, consult driveOk root and return Dropped if the drive is absent, otherwise Deterministic. Keep UserError and the other types as they are.
verdict.fix_risk: This is low risk. With the drive present the verdict is unchanged, so RemovableTests caseDeterministic (PermissionDenied with drive present, one call, no output) still holds. A genuine ACL refusal that coincides with the drive being absent will now wait for the drive before rethrowing, which is harmless. The fix does not help when the device returns 31 while root-id.json is still readable. Adding one driveOk read on that path is negligible.

confirmed.title: No top-level exception handler: any escaped IOException exits with 1 ('差异/待处理'), not the documented 2 ('IO 失败')
confirmed.summary: main runs `code <- run cmd` with no catch. Every exception that escapes a command goes to GHC's default top handler, which prints 'pm: <exception>' to stderr and exits with code 1. DESIGN §5.1 defines 1 as 'differences / degraded / plan pending / partial conflict' and 2 as 'error (… IO 失败)'. The project knows escapes happen by design ('执行期写口逃逸 = §6.4 进程死亡语义', DESIGN.md:610). It has also recognised escape-with-exit-1 as a defect at one site (Commands.hs:395-398, C102 'exit 1 与「清干净但有 HELD」同码，调用方分不清'), but it fixed only that loop and never the class at the process boundary.
confirmed.failure_scenario: (1) `pm backup --apply --yes`: the backup drive drops mid-execution and does not return within drive-wait. execPlanRetry rethrows (`unless ok (throwIO e)`, Removable.hs:254), the exception passes through executePlanNow' / savePlanAndMaybeRunTo / runBackupDiff with no handler, and pm exits 1. That is the same code as a run that completed with some CONFLICT items or an incomplete-scan verdict. A script or wrapper that treats 1 as 'look at the report' and 2 as 'failed, run pm doctor' will not notice that the batch was abandoned with dangling Intents. (2) `pm scan`: scanning succeeds but saveCatalog throws (for example, rotating catalog.json.1 fails after the sharing-violation retry budget because an AV or backup tool holds it). pm exits 1, the same code as 'scan finished with volatile/unreadable files', and the summary line is never printed.
confirmed.evidence:

```
main = do
  setupConsole
  suppressCriticalErrorDialogs
  cmd <- execParser parserInfo
  code <- run cmd
  if code == 0 then exitSuccess else exitWith (ExitFailure code)
```

confirmed.title: withDriveRetry around loadCatalog cannot fire: a drive drop or media hiccup becomes 'no snapshot' and pm backup silently re-hashes the whole backup drive
confirmed.summary: runBackupDiff reads the backup catalog with `withDriveRetry dw broot "读备份索引" (loadCatalog broot)`. loadCatalog never throws for these conditions; it turns them into values. A vanished drive letter makes GetFileAttributes return error 3. probeName maps that to NameMissing, requirePmTrusted passes, readPmState returns Right Nothing for all three generations, and the result is CatAbsent with no warning. A transient read error on a present drive becomes readPmState Left, which loadCatalog' tags with tamperMark (ending the fallback chain), and the result is CatRefused. In both cases withDriveRetry sees success and never waits or retries. oldBak becomes Nothing, and scanRootRetry then re-hashes every file on the backup drive. The REVIEW-LOG 1.1.2 entry says this wrapper protects catalog reads and that the drop protection exists to avoid exactly this ('每次掉线白读几十 GB').
confirmed.failure_scenario: The backup drive is present when runBackupRun' discovers it (discoverBackupRoot plus requireRole read root-id.json). It then drops, or has a read hiccup, while runBackupRun' runs mainFresh over the whole main library and before line 223 runs. Two outcomes: (a) the drive letter is gone, so loadCatalog broot returns CatAbsent with no message; or (b) catalog.json gets an I/O error, so the user sees '⚠ 备份快照损坏已跳过: …无法可信读取…，快照拒绝载入 → pm scan 重建', which is misleading because the snapshot is intact. scanRootRetry's ensureDrive then waits for the drive to return and scans with an empty seed. Every file on the backup drive is hashed again, possibly hundreds of GB over USB, taking hours, and this sustained I/O is what the project's own records identify as the trigger for further drops. The final catalog is correct, so there is no data loss. The cost is the one the 1.1.2 feature was built to prevent, and it happens silently. The same pattern appears at BackupCmd.hs:267 (post-apply lb2 read → '备份缓存未刷新（备份盘尚无索引）') and inside Cli.writeBackCatalog (loadCatalog → CatAbsent → catalog write-back silently skipped with '尚无索引').
confirmed.evidence:
src/Pm/BackupCmd.hs:223-226:
```
(oldBak, bwarns) <- catalogMaybe <$> withDriveRetry dw broot "读备份索引" (loadCatalog broot)
mapM_ (\w -> putStrLn ("⚠ 备份快照损坏已跳过: " <> w)) bwarns
...
result <- scanRootRetry dw ScanOpts {...} oldBak (riId info) broot
```
Removable.withDriveRetry (Removable.hs:161-172) only acts on `Left e` from `try act`. Config.readPmState (Config.hs:336-347) catches IOException: isDoesNotExistError → Right Nothing, any other → Left. Catalog.loadCatalog' (Catalog.hs:131-137): `Right Nothing -> pure (Nothing, warns)`; `Left m -> pure (Nothing, warns <> [m <> tamperMark])`. classify (Nothing, []) = CatAbsent. Win.fileAttrs (Win.hs:212) maps error 2/3 to 'missing'. Probes on this machine: canonicalizePath "Q:\\Photography" returns the path without throwing, and GetFileAttributesW on a path under a non-existent drive gives GetLastError()=3. Scan.scanRoot (Scan.hs:304): `oldEntries = maybe Map.empty catEntries oldCat`, so every file is hashed. By contrast the Removable module doc says boolean probes must be preceded by ensureDrive because 'doesFileExist 在盘不在时答 False'. No ensureDrive precedes line 223.

verdict.reasoning:
Traced against the code. The mechanism is correct at line 223. The sub-claim about Cli.writeBackCatalog is wrong.

(1) Line 223 wraps only `loadCatalog broot` in withDriveRetry. withDriveRetry (Removable.hs:161-172) acts only on `Left e` from `try act`. loadCatalog never throws for either of the two conditions:
- Drive letter gone. requirePmTrusted (Config.hs:262-289) calls resolveUnder root ".pm". canonicalizePath does not throw; my probe `canonicalizePath "Q:/Photography"` printed "Q:\\Photography". probeName then hits GetFileAttributes error 3, which fileAttrs (Win.hs:212-217) maps to Right Nothing, i.e. NameMissing, and that is Right (). loadCatalog' then calls readPmState (Config.hs:333-347): resolveUnder yields Just (a missing component is allowed), and openBoundTo → openBinaryFile throws. My probe `openBinaryFile "Q:/Photography/.pm/catalog.json" ReadMode` gave `(True, does not exist, ...)`, so isDoesNotExistError holds and the result is Right Nothing. All three generations come back as Right Nothing, so classify (Nothing, []) = CatAbsent (Catalog.hs:94). No warning is printed.
- Transient read error with the drive present. readPmState returns Left "…无法可信读取…". loadCatalog' appends tamperMark (Catalog.hs:133) and stops the chain, giving CatRefused. Line 224 prints '⚠ 备份快照损坏已跳过: …快照拒绝载入 → pm scan 重建', which is misleading.

In both cases catalogMaybe gives oldBak = Nothing. scanRootRetry (Removable.hs:200-218) runs ensureDrive, which waits for the drive, then calls scanRoot with old = Nothing. Every file on the backup drive is re-hashed. saveCatalog rotates the old catalog to .1 and the final catalog is correct, so there is no data loss and no wrong diff. bwarns do not enter backupVerdict, so the exit code is unaffected.

The window is real. Between requireRole (which reads root-id.json and proves the drive is present) and line 223, runBackupRun' runs loadCatalog on main and mainFresh. mainFresh (Cli.hs:500-506) is a freshnessSweep over the whole main library, a stat walk lasting seconds or more, not a millisecond race.

This breaks the module's own rule. The Removable.hs header for ensureDrive says boolean probes must be preceded by ensureDrive because an absent drive reads as 'absent'. It also contradicts the 1.1.2 intent in REVIEW-LOG.md:599, which says withDriveRetry wraps the catalog reads and names `runBackupDiff（读索引 / …）`. Nothing in REVIEW-LOG, the findings JSON or DESIGN rules this intended. The closest prior item is the refuted 'execPlanRetry ignores readJournal's error list' entry (findings JSON ~1650-1670). It has the same inert-wrapper shape, but it was refuted because no outcome was reachable except through a millisecond window. Here a seconds-long window leads to a concrete multi-hour full re-hash over USB. So this is not a duplicate.

(2) Line 267 (post-apply lb2): the same mechanism applies. The only effect is the message '⚠ 备份缓存未刷新（备份盘尚无索引）' and a skipped rebuildable cache refresh, which is cosmetic.

(3) The Cli.writeBackCatalog sub-claim is refuted. writeBackCatalog runs inside withRootLock (Cli.hs:274). withRootLock first calls `createDirectoryIfMissing True (pmDir root)` and then openStateLock (Config.hs:556-568), and both throw on an absent drive before loadCatalog runs. judgeIO then sees driveOk False, returns Dropped, and withDriveRetry at Cli.hs:157 does fire.

Severity: no data loss and a correct final result. The cost is the wasted full re-hash that the 1.1.2 feature exists to prevent, plus a misleading 'snapshot damaged' message in case (b). The trigger is a drop or hiccup in a short idle window, so I rate it low.
verdict.corrected_summary: In runBackupDiff, `withDriveRetry dw broot "读备份索引" (loadCatalog broot)` (BackupCmd.hs:223) is inert. loadCatalog turns an absent drive into CatAbsent: canonicalizePath does not throw, GetFileAttributes error 3 gives NameMissing, and openBinaryFile gives isDoesNotExistError, so readPmState returns Right Nothing. A transient read error becomes CatRefused through tamperMark. Neither case throws. If the backup drive drops, or hiccups on catalog.json, in the window after requireRole (during mainFresh's stat sweep of the main library), pm backup silently discards the valid backup snapshot. In the hiccup case it also wrongly reports it as damaged. scanRootRetry then waits for the drive and re-hashes the entire backup drive with an empty seed. The final catalog and diff are still correct and nothing is lost; the cost is the hours of USB I/O that the 1.1.2 drop protection was built to avoid. The same inert wrap at line 267 only produces a misleading 'cache not refreshed (尚无索引)' message. The claimed Cli.writeBackCatalog variant does not exist: withRootLock creates .pm and opens .pm/lock before loadCatalog, and that throws on an absent drive, so its withDriveRetry does fire.
verdict.suggested_fix: Before line 223 (and line 266), call `ensureDrive dw broot "读备份索引"` inside the withDriveRetry action, and after loadCatalog call `requireDrive dw broot "读备份索引"`. The action becomes `ensureDrive dw broot w >> loadCatalog broot >>= \r -> requireDrive dw broot w >> pure r`. A CatAbsent or CatRefused result from a drive that vanished mid-read then turns into a ResourceVanished IOException, which judgeIO classifies as Dropped, so the read waits and retries. Both helpers are no-ops when drive-wait is disabled.
verdict.fix_risk: Low. Both helpers are no-ops under noDriveWait, so behaviour with drive-wait disabled is unchanged. With drive-wait on, a genuinely empty backup drive with root-id.json present still returns CatAbsent, because requireDrive passes. A present-drive read hiccup reported as CatRefused is still not retried: fixing that needs loadCatalog to expose I/O-vs-tamper Left, which touches the trust-gate classification and needs care not to retry real tamper refusals. RemovableTests may need a case that pins the new wait.

confirmed.title: fix #37 regression: CleanShutdown journal append after purge is unguarded; on backup-drive drop it escapes and loses the documented k/N report and exit 2
confirmed.summary: Commit 0decf79 (fix #37) inserted `withJournal root ... jAppend j Barrier . JCleanShutdown` between the per-item-try purge loop and the result reporting in trashEmptyLocked'. The purge loop was deliberately made exception-free (C102: 'escape → exit 1, caller cannot tell 清完 from 删到第 k 个死掉'), but the new journal write is not wrapped in try. When the purge stopped because the medium went away (or the journal is otherwise unwritable), withJournal throws, so neither the '✗ … 已清除 k/N 项，其余未动；…重跑 pm trash empty' line nor the '✓ 已清除 n 项' line is printed and the process exits via GHC's default handler with code 1 instead of the documented 2.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `pm trash empty --backup --yes` on the backup drive E:, which the project's own records say drops out frequently (DESIGN §6.4 note, 11 drops in one day). The drive drops after k>0 payloads were unlinked: deleteBoundAt on item k+1 fails and purgeLoop returns Left (k,p,e). Then `when (k > 0) $ withJournal root ...` runs createDirectoryIfMissing on E:\Photography\.pm, which throws (drive gone). The exception escapes runTrash → Main. Output is 'pm: E:\...: does not exist', exit 1. That code means 'HELD entries remain / needs --yes' in this command's table. The documented partial-purge report (DESIGN.md:260: print ✗ … 已清除 k/N、exit 2) is lost. Before 0decf79 this path printed the report and returned 2. The same escape happens on the success path (Right n) if the drive drops after the last unlink: the deletions happened but the user sees a crash.
confirmed.evidence:
src/Pm/Commands.hs:403-418:
```
done <- purgeLoop (0 :: Int) purgeable
-- 2026-09-25 审计 #37 ...
when (either (\(k, _, _) -> k) id done > 0) $
  withJournal root $ \j -> getCurrentTime >>= jAppend j Barrier . JCleanShutdown
case done of
  Right n -> do putStrLn ("✓ 已清除 " ...); pure (...)
  Left (k, p, e) -> do putStrLn ("✗ " <> p <> ... "已清除 " <> show k <> "/" ...); pure 2
```
purgeLoop (Commands.hs:420-425) wraps each deleteBoundAt in `try :: IO (Either IOException ())` so it cannot escape. withJournal (Journal.hs:92-102) does `createDirectoryIfMissing True (pmDir root)` and then `withPmStateAppend'`, which calls ioError/openStateAppendTail; both throw with no handler. The call chain Main `run (CmdTrash ...)` → runTrash → withRootLock → trashEmptyLocked' has no drive-wait wrapper and no catch. The comment at Commands.hs:395-398 records the intended contract: 'exit 2（DESIGN §5：IO 失败 = 2）'. Commit 0decf79 is the only change to this block.

verdict.reasoning:
I read the code and it matches the claim. src/Pm/Commands.hs:399 is `done <- purgeLoop (0 :: Int) purgeable`. purgeLoop (Commands.hs:420-425) wraps each `deleteBoundAt p` in `try ... :: IO (Either IOException ())`, so an unlink failure cannot escape. Commit 0decf79 (fix #37, `git show --stat` shows Commands.hs +9/-1) then added lines 404-405: `when (either (\(k,_,_) -> k) id done > 0) $ withJournal root $ \j -> getCurrentTime >>= jAppend j Barrier . JCleanShutdown`, with no try around it. withJournal (Journal.hs:92-102) runs `createDirectoryIfMissing True (pmDir root)` and then `withPmStateAppend'`, which calls ioError on an untrusted path. jAppend with Barrier calls hPut plus flushHandleToDisk. Any of these can throw.

Nothing up the call chain catches the exception. withRootLock (Config.hs:556-574) only adds `finally hClose h`. runTrash' TrashEmpty (Commands.hs:319-325) and runTrash (274-284) have no handler. The Main.hs:118-122 `run (CmdTrash ...)` branch has no driveWaitFor wrapper, unlike doctor at Main.hs:112. main (Main.hs:95-101) has no catch. So an exception reaches GHC's top-level handler, which prints `pm: <path>: ...` and exits with code 1.

Trace. The backup drive is E:, and DESIGN.md:605 records 11 drops in one day. `pm trash empty --backup --yes` lists N=3 purgeable items. Items 1 and 2 are unlinked. The drive then drops, deleteBoundAt on item 3 throws an IOException, try catches it, and purgeLoop returns `Left (2, p3, e)`. At line 404 k=2>0, so withJournal runs, and createDirectoryIfMissing on E:\...\.pm (or the append open) throws. Lines 406-418 never run. The user does not see `✗ ... 已清除 2/3 项，其余未动；...重跑 pm trash empty`. The process exits 1, which is the code this command uses for 'HELD remain / needs --yes' (lines 377, 386, 409). DESIGN.md:260 documents the partial-purge contract as that ✗ line plus exit 2, and the comment at Commands.hs:392-398 (C102) says the try was added so callers can tell 清完 from 删到第 k 个死掉. Before 0decf79 this path printed the report and returned 2, so the commit is a regression.

The success path is also affected. If all N items are unlinked and the journal append then fails, the user sees a crash even though the purge completed. In both cases CleanShutdown is not written, so the #37 C4 fix is also defeated until the next successful run.

Prior findings: the findings JSON mentions purgeLoop only in the pre-fix #37 context ('never touches the journal'). REVIEW-LOG.md:634 (#37) does not consider the journal write failing. Tests do not cover it: SweepTests caseTrashEmptyUnlinkFailure denies unlink on a present drive, where the journal stays writable, and AuditFixTests #37 covers only the happy path.

Impact: no data loss. The deletions were confirmed, the manifest stays as history, and a rerun is idempotent. What goes wrong is the exit code (1 instead of 2) and the missing k/N summary on an edge path (medium lost mid-purge, or journal unwritable). The drive-drop trigger is realistic for E:, but the harm is limited to reporting. Severity: low.
verdict.corrected_summary: Regression from commit 0decf79 (fix #37). In trashEmptyLocked' (Commands.hs:404-405), the CleanShutdown journal append runs after the exception-safe purgeLoop without any try. If the journal cannot be written after k>0 items were purged (backup drive dropped mid-purge, unwritable `.pm`, untrusted journal path), the IOException escapes through withRootLock, runTrash and Main to GHC's top-level handler. The documented partial-purge report (`✗ ... 已清除 k/N 项 ...`, exit 2; DESIGN.md:260) or the success line is not printed, the process exits 1 (the code for 'HELD remain / needs --yes'), and CleanShutdown is not written either.
verdict.suggested_fix: Wrap the new write in `try`, e.g. `jr <- if k' > 0 then try (withJournal root $ \j -> getCurrentTime >>= jAppend j Barrier . JCleanShutdown) :: IO (Either IOException ()) else pure (Right ())`. Then always run the existing `case done of` report. On `Left e`, also print a line such as `✗ 收尾标记写入失败: <e> —— 下一次 pm doctor 可能把已清除的隔离载荷报成 C4，重跑 pm trash empty 或任一计划可消除` and return 2 (DESIGN §5: IO failure = 2) instead of 0/1 on the Right path.
verdict.fix_risk: Low. Catching IOException only (not SomeException) leaves async exceptions alone. The one behaviour change is that a journal-write failure after a fully successful purge returns exit 2 instead of crashing with 1. Scripts that check for exit 0 are unaffected on the normal path. A test is needed to pin it, e.g. deny write on `.pm/journal.ndjson` after staging a purgeable item and assert the ✗ k/N or ✓ summary line plus exit 2.

confirmed.title: planStale's try is dead code: doesPathExist swallows every error as False, so an unreadable source is judged gone and prune deletes the plan
confirmed.summary: planStale says probe failures count as 'source still there' (fail-closed) and wraps the probe in `try`. But System.Directory.doesPathExist catches every IOError itself and returns False. Any error that is not 'not found' (media/CRC error on a card directory, access denied on a parent, device-not-ready on a subdirectory while the volume root still answers) therefore becomes `not ex && vol` = True. The plan is labelled a stale draft and `pm plan prune` / POST /api/plans/prune deletes it. The GUI also hides its Execute button and shows the 'plan has expired' banner.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The user generates an import/sort plan from a camera card E:, then reads the card in a flaky reader. The volume root `E:\` answers, so doesDirectoryExist (takeDrive src) is True. Looking up `E:\DCIM\100MSDCF\DSC0001.ARW` fails with ERROR_CRC (23) or ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED. doesPathExist returns False instead of throwing, the try never fires, and every source reads as 'gone'. `pm plan list` tags the plan 已失效, the GUI shows 'this plan has expired, execution will only CONFLICT' and removes the Execute button, and `pm plan prune` deletes the plan file. The files are still on the card.
confirmed.evidence: Plan.hs:383-393: `planStale p mr ... sourceGone op = do let src = opSource (plRootPath p) op; r <- try (do ex <- doesPathExist src; vol <- doesDirectoryExist (takeDrive src); pure (not ex && vol)) :: IO (Either IOException Bool); pure (either (const False) id r)`. The doc comment at Plan.hs:381-382 reads '探测抛出一律按「源还在」计（fail-closed：判不出就不判失效，prune 不会因此多删）'. Probe on this machine: `try (doesPathExist "C:/a<b|c")` -> `Right False`, while `getFileSize` on the same path -> `Left ... CreateFile ... invalid argument`: doesPathExist swallows the error and never throws. Consumers: prunePlans Plan.hs:444-445 (`cleanable p = ... else planStale p mr` -> deletePlan), runPlanList Plan.hs:463, GET /api/plans Serve.hs:420 (`stale` field), app.js showPlan `if (allowApply && pending > 0 && !isStale)` hides Execute. The project already has a three-state probe for this (Pm.Win.probeName, NameMissing vs ProbeUnknown). Not covered by known item #7, which concerned the critical-error dialog.

verdict.reasoning: CODE: src/Pm/Plan.hs:389-392 `sourceGone op = do let src = opSource (plRootPath p) op; r <- try (do ex <- doesPathExist src; vol <- doesDirectoryExist (takeDrive src); pure (not ex && vol)) :: IO (Either IOException Bool); pure (either (const False) id r)`. The doc comment at Plan.hs:380-381 promises '探测抛出一律按「源还在」计（fail-closed…prune 不会因此多删）', and DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:590 and REVIEW-LOG.md:603 repeat 探测抛出按「源在」计. LIBRARY: `directory`'s doesPathExist catches every IOError from getFileMetadata and returns False. The project measured this itself (src/Pm/Exec.hs:334: '实测 doesPathExist 自己吞掉这类错误答 False', which is why slotOccupied does not rely on it). I re-probed it here: `try (doesPathExist "C:/a<b|c")` gives `Right False`, while `getFileSize` on the same path gives `Left … invalid argument`. The `try` therefore never fires on the first probe. Any non-not-found error on the source (ACL deny, ERROR_CRC/I/O error on a flaky card, a network error on one subpath) becomes ex=False. The volume-root probe answers True (root cached or reachable), so sourceGone = True. TRACE: never-executed import plan with sources `E:\DCIM\100MSDCF\*.ARW`. The card sits in a flaky reader and GetFileAttributesEx on each file returns an I/O error, but `E:\` answers. Then prunePlans (Plan.hs:444 `cleanable p = … else planStale p mr`) → allM sourceGone → all True → victims include the plan → deletePlan removes .pm/plans/<id>.json. runPlanList (Plan.hs:463) and GET /api/plans (Serve.hs:420) label it 已失效, and the GUI hides Execute. Not a duplicate: #7 in docs/reviews/2026-09-25-full-debug-findings.json covers only the critical-error dialog; its verdict mentions the swallowing in passing but does not rule on it, and no refuted entry covers it. Not ruled intended: the documented contract is the opposite. Mitigations: #7's process-wide SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS means an empty slot now returns an error and the volume probe also fails (vol=False → not stale), so the common card-pulled case stays correct. The trigger needs a mixed state: the root answers but the per-file lookup fails for a reason other than not-found, and it must fail for every pending item. Damage is limited to deleting a plan file, which the design treats as regenerable (Plan.hs:395; journal untouched), and only after the user asks to prune. No photo data is at risk. So the defect is real but low.
verdict.corrected_summary: planStale's fail-closed guard is dead code. doesPathExist (and doesDirectoryExist) in the `directory` package swallow every IOError and return False, so the surrounding `try` never sees a throw. A source that cannot be probed (access denied, device I/O/CRC error, network error) on a volume whose root still answers is judged 'gone'. That contradicts the documented '探测抛出按「源在」计' (Plan.hs:380-381, DESIGN-COMMANDS.md:590). If every pending item is affected, the plan is shown as 已失效 in CLI and GUI (Execute hidden) and `pm plan prune` / POST /api/plans/prune deletes the plan file. Photo data is never touched, and the empty-card-slot case stays correct because #7's error mode makes the volume probe fail too.
verdict.suggested_fix: Replace the boolean probe with a three-state one that only reports gone on a definite not-found. For example, use `Pm.Win.probeName src` and count only `NameMissing` as gone (`NamePlain`/`NameSurrogate`/`ProbeUnknown` → not gone). Alternatively, `try (getSymbolicLinkMetadata src)` with `Left e | isDoesNotExistError e` → gone, any other Left → not gone. Keep the volume check (`doesDirectoryExist (takeDrive src)`) as is: its swallowing errs toward vol=False, which is already conservative.
verdict.fix_risk: probeName uses lstat semantics and does not follow links. A dangling symlink/junction at the source would read as present (not gone), so the draft stays listed as 未执行, which is the conservative direction. probeName may also map path-not-found (ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND, 3) differently from file-not-found (2): if it classes 3 as ProbeUnknown, drafts whose whole card folder was wiped (DCIM/100MSDCF removed) would stop being judged stale, regressing the 1.1.3 behaviour and caseStale's 全缺 segment. Check the error-code mapping (Win.hs:187-196) and rerun PlanExecTests caseStale.

refuted.title: ensureDrive's timeout exception is caught by the enclosing retry loop, which waits a second full drive-wait after announcing '✗ 盘没有回来，放弃重试'
refuted.reason: The trace is accurate. ensureDrive (Removable.hs:178-183) calls recover with Dropped, waits dwWaitSecs, prints '✗ 盘没有回来，放弃重试', and then throws dropError, which has type ResourceVanished (line 193). scanRootRetry's `try` (line 203) catches it. With n < 5, judgeIO sees ResourceVanished outside the deterministic set and driveOk False, so it returns Dropped. recover (line 209) then waits a second dwWaitSecs before throwIO, so the total wait is 2x drive-wait. This re-judging is documented as intended, though. The ensureDrive comment at Removable.hs:175-176 says: '等不到 → 抛一个 ResourceVanished 型异常——不是 userError，外层 withDriveRetry 还能再判一次'. REVIEW-LOG.md:599 describes requireDrive the same way ('ResourceVanished 型，外层再判'). Using ResourceVanished instead of userError was a deliberate choice so the outer retry layer can wait again. The dwWaitSecs field doc (line 67) describes one wait, not a whole-run budget. The only real residue is cosmetic: '放弃重试' is printed by an inner layer and an outer layer then keeps waiting, which is a message-wording issue. Nothing is lost or corrupted; the run only ends later. Because the behaviour is documented as intended and the remainder is cosmetic, I refute it.
